items.summary: You meet Kestrel Health Network, Project Beacon, the people, systems and data files, and the four exams you will pass by building Beacon. You write the programme brief: one page that explains the problem, the three releases, the people and how success is measured.

read.heading: Welcome to Kestrel Health Network
read.body:
Welcome. For the next 13 weeks you work at Kestrel Health Network (KHN), a fictional regional health network in Alberta, Canada. Its data is synthetic and patients are never named; visits carry pseudonymous IDs such as V0001.

Kestrel is a public body and a custodian of health information, so patient health information it holds falls under Alberta's Health Information Act (HIA). It runs four sites in three zones:

| Code | Site | Zone |
|---|---|---|
| KGH | Kestrel General Hospital (busiest emergency department) | Central |
| ARH | Aspen Ridge Hospital | North |
| CVH | Coulee Valley Hospital | South |
| PGH | Prairie Gate Health Centre (rural) | Central |

You are Beacon's Programme Manager. Three problems brought you here:

1. Emergency department (ED) and patient-flow leaders work from Excel extracts emailed each morning. Sites' numbers disagree, nobody trusts them, and the extracts carry more patient detail than anyone needs.
2. Clinicians wait days for access, while agency nurses and vendor engineers keep accounts long after they leave. Nobody can prove who can see what.
3. A ransomware attack on another (fictional) hospital made the board ask whether care could continue if clinical systems went down. Nobody has tested a restore of the Clinical Information System in over a year.

read.heading: Project Beacon: one programme, three releases
read.body:
Beacon has one charter, budget, schedule and change-control board. It runs from 1 September to 17 December 2026: 78 working days, Monday to Friday. Each of its three releases uses all four exams, because real work does: a dashboard needs a plan, access control and support.

| Release | Study weeks | What it delivers | Gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Patient-flow analytics service | 1 to 6 | De-identified Power BI dashboards for ED flow and beds, run as a supported service | Go-live 2026-10-23; PL-300 and ITIL exams week 6 day 4 |
| 2 Clinician identity and access | 6 (day 5) to 10 (day 3) | Role-based access tied to HR events, multi-factor authentication (MFA), single sign-on, access reviews | Acceptance 2026-11-26; PMP exam week 10 day 3 |
| 3 Cyber resilience | 10 (day 4) to 13 | Business impact analysis, recovery targets, downtime procedures, incident response, security dashboard, closure | Programme acceptance 2026-12-17; CISSP exam week 13 day 4 |

The budget at completion is CAD 1,200,000 across 15 work packages: Release 1 CAD 420,000, Release 2 CAD 460,000, Release 3 CAD 320,000. The sponsor holds a management reserve of CAD 120,000 outside the register, so total authorized funding is CAD 1,320,000. Programme-wide documents (charter, schedule, RAID log of risks, assumptions, issues and decisions, change control) live in Release 1.

read.heading: How the 13 weeks work
read.body:
Each session has three parts: read the lesson, build today's part of Beacon, check yourself.

- Today shows the session. Start opens focus mode with a timer and this lesson. Mark done completes it.
- Learn holds every lesson, the four exam guides, the writing guide and finished example for every document, and the glossary.
- Project shows every document with How to write it, See the finished example, a Done when checklist, a writing area, Explain it in your own words, and Check yourself (five questions).
- Practice has Scenarios, Timed set (15 minutes, recorded as evidence), Review, Flashcards and Labs.
- Progress shows four readiness scores: coverage 30, documents 35, judgment 25, recall 10.

Before each exam gate, Progress runs five checks: (1) every session before the gate is done; (2) every document in the releases up to the gate is complete; (3) two timed sets for that exam at 80% or better; (4) at least 24 decisions recorded for that exam with under 30% wrong; (5) no open wrong answers and at least 6 written explanations of 80 characters or more. Sit the exam only when all five are met.

read.heading: Exam rules you can rely on
read.body:
PMP (from PMI). 180 questions (170 scored, 10 unscored pretest), 240 minutes, two 10-minute breaks, at a test centre or online proctored. Eligibility: experience within the last 10 years in non-overlapping months (two projects in one month count once), plus 35 contact hours of project management training (waived for active Certified Associate in Project Management, CAPM, holders).

Months needed: secondary school 60; associate's or post-secondary vocational 48; bachelor's or equivalent 36; bachelor's or postgraduate from a PMI GAC-accredited program 24.

From 1 December 2026, live instructor-led training counts toward the 35 hours only if a PMI Authorized Training Partner, a China Registered Education Provider or an eligible accredited higher-education program delivers it. Renew with 60 professional development units (PDUs) every 3 years.

PL-300 (Microsoft Certified: Power BI Data Analyst Associate). 100 minutes, pass at 700 (scaled), proctored by Pearson VUE, may include interactive components; no fixed question count is published. Microsoft sets no formal experience requirement, but expects you to be proficient with Power Query and DAX (Data Analysis Expressions). Renew every 12 months with a free online assessment on Microsoft Learn. Retake after 24 hours following a first failed attempt.

CISSP (from ISC2). English exams are adaptive: 100 to 150 items in 3 hours, pass at 700 of 1000, no going back. You need at least five years of cumulative, full-time, paid work in two or more of the eight domains; a four-year degree or an approved credential waives one year. Pass without it and you become an Associate of ISC2, with six years to gain the experience. After passing you need endorsement by an ISC2-certified professional in good standing. Maintain with 120 continuing professional education (CPE) credits per 3-year cycle (40 a year) and an annual fee.

ITIL Foundation (Version 5). 40 multiple-choice questions, 60 minutes, closed book, pass at 65% (26 of 40). Online proctoring available, no mandatory training prerequisite, nine languages. Renew every 3 years through continuing professional development (CPD) or a retake. ITIL 4 Foundation holders can take the Foundation Bridge (Version 5).

keyTerms.definition: A group of related projects or releases managed together for benefits none would deliver alone. Beacon is one programme with three releases, one charter, one budget and one change-control board.
A planned, accepted delivery of working capability. Beacon's releases are patient-flow analytics, clinician identity and access, and cyber resilience, each closed by a gate.
The point in the study plan where you sit an exam, only after Progress shows all five readiness checks met. Gates fall in week 6 day 4, week 10 day 3 and week 13 day 4.

Under the Health Information Act, a body or health professional listed in the Act or designated by regulation, responsible for the health information it holds. Kestrel is a custodian and stays responsible for its affiliates, such as employees and contractors.
The senior leader who funds and champions the programme and approves its charter. For Beacon this is Dr. Helen Marchetti (E-001), VP Clinical Operations.
A one-page orientation that states the problem, the releases, the people and the success measures, so anyone can understand Beacon in two minutes.

build.goal: Write the Beacon programme brief: one page that a new team member or a board member can read in two minutes and understand the problem, the releases, the people and the measures of success.
steps: Open Project, Release 1: Patient-flow analytics service, then Programme brief. Read How to write it and See the finished example before you type anything.

In the problem section, write the three problems in plain words and give each one fact from the charter baselines: KGH median 80.5 minutes from arrival to physician initial assessment; access requests resolved within 72 hours 27.3%; CIS restore tests failed at 9.0 and 13.5 hours against a 4-hour target.

In the releases section, build a table with the three releases: what each delivers in one line and its gate (go-live 2026-10-23, acceptance 2026-11-26, programme acceptance 2026-12-17). Add one line saying Beacon has one charter, one budget, one schedule and one change-control board.

In the people section, list the sponsor, the change-control chair, the Chief Privacy Officer, the Chief Information Security Officer, the service desk manager, the analytics lead and the two business owners with their E-IDs and what each decides, then add yourself as Programme Manager.
In the success section, list the nine charter measures with baseline (data) and target (agreed with the sponsor), and say they are measured three months after each release.

Add a budget and timeline section (budget at completion CAD 1,200,000: Release 1 CAD 420,000, Release 2 CAD 460,000, Release 3 CAD 320,000; management reserve CAD 120,000; total CAD 1,320,000; 78 working days), the top risks with IDs and owners (R-01, R-02, R-04, R-08), the open issues I-01 to I-03, and a few bullets on how Beacon is run.
Check every item on the Done when checklist and write two sentences in Explain it in your own words.
build.modelAnswer: A good brief fits on one page and uses Kestrel's own words. It opens with the three problems, each backed by one number. A release table gives scope and gate date, and the budget section adds the three releases to CAD 1,200,000, with the CAD 120,000 reserve shown separately. It names each owner with an E-ID. It separates data baselines from agreed targets. It never uses PIA for anything except physician initial assessment.

examTips.tip: People domain, task 1 Develop a common vision: when a question describes a team or sponsor who disagree about what the project is for, the best answer usually builds shared understanding of the vision and outcomes before any plan or tool choice.

The exam is 100 minutes and may include interactive components, so practise in Power BI Desktop itself. Prepare the data, Model the data and Visualize and analyze the data each carry 25–30%, so every Release 1 build counts.

The adaptive format means you cannot go back. Practise answering as a risk advisor to management, not as a technician. Security and Risk Management is the heaviest domain at 16%, and Beacon's charter and business case practise it from week 1.

Foundation is 40 questions in 60 minutes, so you have 90 seconds each. Learn the seven guiding principles by name; Focus on value is the one this week's brief practises, because it starts from the outcomes clinicians and patients need.

pitfalls: Writing a charter instead of a brief. The brief orients readers; it does not authorize work, set authority or replace the charter you write on day 5.
Presenting targets as data. Baselines such as 5.7% LWBS come from the data; targets such as 4.5% are agreed with the sponsor and must be labelled that way.
Abbreviating the privacy impact assessment. Always write it in full, because at Kestrel PIA means physician initial assessment only.
Listing technology (Power BI, MFA) as the goal. Lead with outcomes for patients, clinicians and the board, then show the technology as the means.

check.q: Why does Beacon run as one programme instead of three separate projects?
check.a: The three releases share people, systems, governance and money. One charter, one budget of CAD 1,200,000 plus a CAD 120,000 reserve, one schedule and one change-control board let Kestrel trade off scope, time and cost across releases and report one set of benefits.

check.q: What must happen before you sit the PL-300 and ITIL Foundation exams in week 6?
check.a: Progress must show all five checks met: every earlier session done, every Release 1 document complete, two timed sets for that exam at 80% or better, at least 24 recorded decisions with under 30% wrong, and no open wrong answers with at least 6 written explanations of 80 characters or more.

check.q: A colleague has a bachelor's degree from a program that is not GAC-accredited, 30 months of non-overlapping project experience in the last 10 years and 35 contact hours. Can they apply for the PMP?
check.a: Not yet. With a bachelor's or equivalent they need 36 months of non-overlapping experience in the last 10 years. The 24-month route applies only to a bachelor's or postgraduate degree from a PMI GAC-accredited program. They need 6 more months.

items.summary: You learn all four exam blueprints in full: the 26 PMP tasks, the PL-300 skill areas, the eight CISSP domains and the ITIL Foundation (Version 5) syllabus. You build the coverage map that shows which Beacon document practises each one.

read.heading: How to read a blueprint
read.body:
A blueprint lists what an exam tests and how much each part weighs: PMI's PMP Examination Content Outline, Microsoft's PL-300 study guide, the ISC2 CISSP exam outline and the ITIL learning objectives. The weight tells you where the marks are. The verb tells you what you must do: Plan and manage risk means choosing the right action in a scenario, not reciting a definition.

Worked example: of PMP's 170 scored questions, People is about 170 x 0.33 = 56, Process about 170 x 0.41 = 70 and Business Environment about 170 x 0.26 = 44. These are planning estimates, not a published split.

read.heading: PL-300: four skill areas
read.body:
Prepare the data (25–30%). Beacon: data-quality workbook.
- Get or connect: sources or a shared semantic model; source settings, credentials and privacy levels; choose Direct Lake, DirectQuery or Import; parameters.
- Profile and clean: statistics and column properties; inconsistencies, unexpected or null values, quality issues; import errors.
- Transform and load: data types; create and transform columns; group and aggregate; pivot, unpivot, transpose; semi-structured data to a table; fact and dimension tables; reference versus duplicate queries; merge and append; relationship keys; data loading.

Model the data (25–30%). Beacon: star schema, DAX catalogue.
- Design: table and column properties; role-playing dimensions; cardinality and cross-filter direction; a common date table; calculated columns and tables.
- DAX: single aggregation measures; CALCULATE; time intelligence; basic statistics; semi-additive measures; quick measures; calculated tables or columns; calculation groups.
- Optimize: remove unneeded rows and columns; Performance Analyzer and DAX query view for poor measures, relationships and visuals; reduce granularity.

Visualize and analyze the data (25–30%). Beacon: reports and dashboards.
- Reports: visuals, formatting, Copilot narratives and pages, themes, conditional formatting, slicing and filtering, page setup, paginated reports, visual calculations.
- Usability and storytelling: bookmarks, tooltips, interactions, navigation, sorting, sync slicers, Selection pane, drillthrough, export settings, mobile, personalization, accessibility, automatic page refresh.
- Patterns and trends: Analyze, grouping, binning, clustering, AI visuals, reference lines, error bars, forecasting, outliers, Copilot summaries.

Manage and secure Power BI (15–20%). Beacon: deployment plan, row-level security (RLS) test pack.
- Workspaces and assets: workspaces, apps, publishing, dashboards, distribution, subscriptions and alerts, promote or certify, gateways, scheduled refresh.
- Secure and govern: workspace roles, item-level access, semantic model access, RLS roles and membership, sensitivity labels.

read.heading: ITIL Foundation (Version 5)
read.body:
Nine learning objectives: digital product and service management concepts; value co-creation; the four dimensions; the ITIL Value System; the guiding principles; the product and service lifecycle; management practices; continual improvement; value stream mapping and management. Version 5 is described as AI-native and unifies digital product and service management.

- Four dimensions: Organizations and People; Information and Technology; Partners and Suppliers; Value Streams and Processes.
- Value System: guiding principles, governance, value chain activities, management practices, continual improvement.
- Seven guiding principles: Focus on value; Start where you are; Progress iteratively with feedback; Collaborate and promote visibility; Think and work holistically; Keep it simple and practical; Optimize and automate.
- Practices: Version 5 keeps ITIL 4's practices with adjustments and new groupings.
- Continual improvement: Version 5 refines the ITIL 4 seven-question model (What is the vision? through How do we keep the momentum going?).

The eight-stage lifecycle replaces ITIL 4's service value chain as the organizing model. Beacon touches each stage: Discover (eliciting leaders' needs), Design (star schema, catalogue entry), Acquire (the Lumen Analytics Partners contract), Build (semantic model and reports), Transition (go-live and support handover), Operate (refresh and gateway), Deliver (leaders using the dashboards), Support (service desk knowledge and escalation).

keyTerms.definition: PMI's published PMP blueprint. The July 2026 outline has three domains (People, Process, Business Environment) and 26 tasks.
The share of the exam a domain or skill area carries, such as Process 41% for PMP or Security and Risk Management 16% for CISSP. Use it to plan study hours.
Microsoft's top-level grouping of what PL-300 measures: Prepare the data, Model the data, Visualize and analyze the data, Manage and secure Power BI.
A numbered heading inside a CISSP domain, such as 5.5 identity and access provisioning lifecycle, that names a topic the exam can test.
ITIL Version 5's eight-stage organizing model: Discover, Design, Acquire, Build, Transition, Operate, Deliver, Support.
A table that links every exam task, skill or domain to the Beacon document and session where you practise it, so gaps show before a gate.

build.goal: Build the exam-to-project coverage map: tables that link every PMP task, PL-300 skill area, CISSP domain and ITIL syllabus item to the Beacon document and session that practises it.
steps: Open Project, Release 1, Exam-to-project coverage map. Read How to write it and See the finished example.

PMP: three tables, People (33%), Process (41%) and Business Environment (26%), with one row per task: task number and exact name, Beacon document and session code. For example, Business Environment 3 Manage and control changes maps to the Change-control process at W2 D5 and W7 D5. That makes 26 rows in all.

PL-300: one row per skill area with its weight and its skill groups in brackets, for example Prepare the data, 25–30% (connect, profile, clean, transform, load), then the Beacon documents and sessions.
CISSP: eight rows with domain number, name and weight, the Beacon documents and sessions. ITIL: nine rows, one per learning objective, each with a Beacon document and session.
Use the session list in Today and Learn to fill the session column, and use document names exactly as Project shows them.

In Gates, gaps and review, name the three gates, mark any objective with only one session or only a session after its gate (such as ITIL value stream mapping at W8 D1), and say on which day you will repair it. Then complete Done when and Check yourself.
build.modelAnswer: Good coverage maps have no blank rows. All 26 PMP task names appear exactly as published, in three tables whose domain weights add to 100%. Each PL-300 skill area, CISSP domain and ITIL learning objective points to at least one document and session. Weak spots are named honestly with a repair plan, such as ITIL value stream mapping, which is built at W8 D1, after the week 6 gate, so it gets extra practice in the ITIL value-stream lab before the exam.

examTips.tip: Process is 41% of the exam, but many Process questions are framed as People or Business Environment situations. Read for the task being tested: a late request is Business Environment 3 Manage and control changes, not Process 2 scope.

Prepare the data, Model the data and Visualize and analyze the data are each 25–30%. Manage and secure Power BI is only 15–20%, but its RLS and workspace-role questions come up again in Beacon's Release 2 and CISSP Identity and Access Management.

Domain 1 Security and Risk Management (16%) frames the whole exam: the best answer usually protects people and the organization first, follows governance and law, then picks a technical control. Learn the 1.x sub-domain headings as your checklist.

Version 5 questions use the eight lifecycle stages. If an option uses ITIL 4 value chain words such as obtain/build or design and transition as if current, treat it with suspicion; the stages are Discover, Design, Acquire, Build, Transition, Operate, Deliver, Support.

pitfalls: Paraphrasing task names. Use the exact published wording, because exam questions and your coverage map both depend on recognizing the task.
Mapping only to documents you like. Domains you avoid, such as CISSP Software Development Security, are exactly where the coverage score will fall short.
Mixing ITIL versions. The eight stages replace the ITIL 4 service value chain as the organizing model; do not list plan, engage or obtain/build as Version 5 stages.

Treating weights as exact question counts. Weights guide study time. PL-300 has no published question count and CISSP's adaptive exam varies from 100 to 150 items, so any per-domain count is only an estimate.

check.q: Which PMP domain and task does the Beacon change-control process practise, and what weight does that domain carry?
check.a: Business Environment, task 3 Manage and control changes. Business Environment carries 26% of the exam. The charter's governance and the change-control board also practise Business Environment 1 Define and establish project governance.

check.q: Name the four PL-300 skill areas with their weights, and say which one Release 1's RLS test pack practises.
check.a: Prepare the data 25–30%; Model the data 25–30%; Visualize and analyze the data 25–30%; Manage and secure Power BI 15–20%. The RLS test pack practises Manage and secure Power BI, in its secure and govern sub-skills (RLS roles and group membership).

check.q: List the eight ITIL Version 5 lifecycle stages in order and give a Beacon example for Transition.
check.a: Discover, Design, Acquire, Build, Transition, Operate, Deliver, Support. Transition in Beacon is Release 1's go-live readiness and support handover, when the dashboards move into live use with the service desk ready to support them.

items.summary: You learn how Kestrel measures emergency care, how to profile a source in Power Query, and why the extract is health information that must be minimized. You profile khn_ed_visits.csv, find every deliberate problem by row ID, and start the data-quality workbook.

read.heading: The extract: 480 rows, ten columns
read.body:
khn_ed_visits.csv holds one row per emergency department (ED) visit from 1 July to 30 September 2026, taken from the ED Tracking Board (A-002) through the Clinical Data Warehouse (A-010).

| Column | Meaning | Kestrel rule |
|---|---|---|
| visit_id | Pseudonymous visit ID, the key | Unique |
| site_code | KGH, ARH, CVH or PGH | Upper case |
| arrival_datetime | Arrival and registration; starts every ED clock | Real date |

read.heading: How Kestrel measures emergency care
read.body:
CTAS assigns each patient a level at triage, each with a time-to-physician objective. The guidelines call these objectives, not established care standards.

| Level | Name | Objective |
|---|---|---|
| I | Resuscitation | Immediate |
| II | Emergent | 15 minutes or less |
| III | Urgent | 30 minutes or less |
| IV | Less Urgent (Semi urgent) | 1 hour or less |
| V | Non Urgent | 2 hours or less |

Fractile response is the share of visits at a level seen within its objective; the guidelines set 95% for Level II and 80% for Level V. The 2016 revision adds an overall benchmark: triage to physician initial assessment, median 1 hour and 90th percentile 3 hours.

Kestrel's own definitions follow the approach of the Canadian Institute for Health Information (CIHI):
- The ED clock starts at arrival_datetime (registration), which in Kestrel's data is never after triage.
- Time to PIA = pia_datetime minus arrival_datetime.
- ED length of stay (LOS) = departure_datetime minus arrival_datetime.
- LWBS = a visit that left before physician initial assessment (disposition LWBS).
- % PIA within CTAS target = visits seen at or under their level's objective (0, 15, 30, 60, 120 minutes) over visits with a valid time to PIA.

Approved Q3 figures: 474 valid visits, 27 LWBS (5.7%), median 64.0 minutes to PIA (KGH 80.5), 28.3% within target. Kestrel measures from arrival and the CTAS benchmark from triage, so always state your clock.

read.heading: Profiling in Power Query
read.body:
Profiling means measuring data before you trust it. In the Power Query Editor, the View tab has three options:
- Column quality: the share of Valid, Error and Empty values.
- Column distribution: distinct values (how many different values) and unique values (values that appear exactly once).
- Column profile: statistics for the selected column (count, errors, empties, distinct, unique, min, max, and for numbers the average and standard deviation) plus a value distribution chart.

By default these use the top 1,000 rows. The status bar reads Column profiling based on top 1000 rows; select it and choose Column profiling based on entire data set. This 480-row file fits the sample by chance; a full year of visits would not, and a bad row at row 5,000 would stay invisible. Switch every time.

After you set explicit types, the raw file shows this (computed from the CSV):

| Column | What the profile shows | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| visit_id | 478 distinct, 476 unique | Two IDs appear twice |
| site_code | 5 distinct, including kgh | A case problem |
| arrival_datetime | 1 error (under 1%) | Not a real date |
| ctas_level | Min 0, max 6 | Values outside 1 to 5 |
| pia_datetime | 27 empty (about 6%) | Expected only for LWBS |
| departure_datetime | 1 empty (under 1%) | A missing departure |

Power Query compares text case-sensitively, which is why kgh counts as its own value.

read.heading: Every deliberate problem, by row
read.body:
| Problem | Rows | Rule | Handling |
|---|---|---|---|
| Exact duplicates (extracts overlapped) | V0315, V0318 | DQ-01 | Remove the second copy |
| Site code in lower case | V0140, V0309 | DQ-03 | Convert to KGH and keep |
| CTAS outside 1 to 5 | V0070 (6), V0222 (0) | DQ-05 | Quarantine; owner corrects from triage record |
| PIA before triage | V0385 | DQ-06 | Keep in counts; null time to PIA and LOS |
| PIA before arrival | V0421 | DQ-06 | Same as V0385 |
| No departure, not LWBS | V0268 | DQ-06 | Keep; null LOS only |
| Invalid date 2026-09-31 | V0476 | DQ-04 | Quarantine; cannot be placed in time |
| LWBS with a PIA time | V0075 | DQ-07 | Quarantine; either field may be wrong |

The reconciliation: 480 source rows, less 2 duplicates, gives 478 unique; less 4 quarantined (V0476, V0070, V0222, V0075) gives 474 valid visits. Quarantined rows are evidence (DQ-13): they go to an exception table with their rule ID and are never deleted.

read.heading: Flag problems without deleting evidence
read.body:
Do not filter bad rows away while profiling. Add a column that names each problem so every row stays visible. Paste this into Home, Advanced Editor and change the file path.

```
let
    Source = Csv.Document(File.Contents("C:\Beacon\khn_ed_visits.csv"), [Delimiter = ","]),
    Promoted = Table.PromoteHeaders(Source, [PromoteAllScalars = true]),
    Typed = Table.TransformColumnTypes(
        Promoted,
        {
            {"visit_id", type text}, {"site_code", type text},
            {"arrival_datetime", type datetime}, {"ctas_level", Int64.Type},
            {"triage_datetime", type datetime}, {"pia_datetime", type datetime},
            {"disposition", type text}, {"departure_datetime", type datetime},
            {"age_band", type text}, {"arrival_mode", type text}
        },
        "en-CA"
    ),
    Flagged = Table.AddColumn(
        Typed,
        "dq_issue",
        each
            if (try [arrival_datetime])[HasError] then "DQ-04 invalid date"
            else if [ctas_level] < 1 or [ctas_level] > 5 then "DQ-05 CTAS out of range"
            else if [disposition] = "LWBS" and [pia_datetime] <> null then "DQ-07 LWBS with PIA"
            else if [pia_datetime] <> null
                and ([pia_datetime] < [arrival_datetime] or [pia_datetime] < [triage_datetime])
                then "DQ-06 PIA out of order"
            else if [disposition] <> "LWBS" and [departure_datetime] = null then "DQ-06 no departure"
            else if [site_code] <> Text.Upper([site_code]) then "DQ-03 lower-case site"
            else null,
        type nullable text
    )
in
    Flagged
```

Filter dq_issue to non-blank and you see 9 rows: V0476, V0070, V0222, V0075, V0385, V0421, V0268, V0140 and V0309. The try expression catches V0476's bad arrival before any comparison uses it. For duplicates, select visit_id and use Home, Keep Rows, Keep Duplicates: 4 rows (V0315 and V0318, twice each). Week 3 turns these flags into the cleaning pipeline.

read.heading: Why this is health information
read.body:
The extract records the emergency care individual patients received, so Kestrel treats it as patient health information under the Health Information Act (HIA), even without names. Two duties decide what it may contain:
- Highest degree of anonymity (section 57): collect, use or disclose health information with the highest degree of anonymity possible, and first consider whether aggregate health information is adequate.
- Least amount (section 58): collect, use or disclose only the amount of health information that is essential for the intended purpose.

Apply them column by column: every field must trace to a measure or requirement. The extract has no names, health numbers, addresses, dates of birth or free text; it uses age bands and a pseudonymous visit_id. If no requirement uses arrival_mode or age_band, drop them too.

Pseudonymous is not anonymous. Minute-level times at a small site can point to one person: Prairie Gate Health Centre had 55 valid visits in Q3, so a chart by day and CTAS level could show a count of 1. That is risk R-02, owned by Priya Raman (E-003). Kestrel's policy, not a law, is to suppress counts under 5 in any report shared outside the care team. So the model keeps pseudonymous rows behind access controls, and dashboards show aggregates. Section 60 adds the duty to keep administrative, technical and physical safeguards around it.

keyTerms.definition: Power Query's quality, distribution and profile views. They use the top 1,000 rows unless you switch the status bar to Column profiling based on entire data set.
Distinct counts how many different values a column holds; unique counts values that appear exactly once. A key column should have both equal to the row count.
Moving a row that fails a classifying rule (bad date, bad CTAS, contradiction) into an exception table with its rule ID, so it is kept as evidence but not counted.
Kestrel's measure of minutes from arrival_datetime to pia_datetime, where PIA means physician initial assessment. Null when either time is missing or the order is impossible.

Health Information Act duties in sections 58 and 57: collect, use or disclose only the health information essential to the purpose, with the highest degree of anonymity possible, considering aggregate data first.
Data where direct identifiers are replaced by a code such as V0001. It can still be re-identified when combined with times, places or small counts, so it stays protected.

examTips.tip: Prepare the data, Profile and clean the data: expect questions on evaluating data with column statistics and properties. Remember that column profiling uses the top 1,000 rows until you choose entire data set, a classic reason a problem is missed.

Prepare the data, resolving import errors and null values: errors from a type change sit in cells, so Keep Errors or a try expression finds them. Replacing errors with null hides evidence; the auditable answer keeps and logs them.

Asset Security, 2.1 identify and classify information and assets and 2.6 data security controls: the data owner (here the Emergency Medical Director) sets classification and use, while custodians and stewards apply controls. Minimization is a control, not only a privacy courtesy.

pitfalls: Profiling only the first 1,000 rows. It feels complete on a small file, then misses problems in a full-year extract.
Deleting bad rows. Quarantine them with a rule ID instead, so the count of 480 still reconciles to 474 plus 4 quarantined plus 2 duplicates.
Dropping V0385 and V0421 from visit counts. Those visits happened; only their durations are unreliable, so keep them in counts and the LWBS rate.
Assuming pseudonymous means anonymous. Small counts at PGH can identify patients, which is why Kestrel suppresses counts under 5 outside the care team.

check.q: The extract has only 480 rows. Why switch profiling to the entire data set anyway?
check.a: Because the default profile uses the top 1,000 rows. It covers this file by chance, but production extracts are larger, and a bad date or CTAS value past row 1,000 would not appear in column quality, distribution or profile. Making the switch a habit protects every later source.

check.q: How should you treat visit V0385, where the physician initial assessment is recorded before triage?
check.a: Under DQ-06, keep the visit in visit counts and the LWBS rate because it happened, but set MinutesToPIA and EDLOSMinutes to null so the impossible order cannot distort the median wait or length of stay. Log it and ask the data owner, Dr. Whitford, for the correct time.

check.q: Which two Health Information Act duties shape the extract, and what do they mean for its columns?
check.a: Section 57 requires the highest degree of anonymity possible, considering aggregate information first, and section 58 allows only the amount of health information essential for the purpose. So every column must trace to a requirement, identifiers stay pseudonymous, age is banded, and anything no requirement uses should be removed.

items.summary: You learn how a business case justifies an investment: the need, options including doing nothing, measurable benefits, costs, reserves and risks. You write the Beacon business case that recommends the full programme to Dr. Helen Marchetti.

read.heading: What a business case does
read.body:
A business case answers one question for the people who fund work: is this worth doing, and which way? It comes before the charter. The business case justifies the investment; the charter, which you write tomorrow, authorizes the programme and gives you authority. A benefits management plan then says how and when each benefit will be measured and who owns it.

A sound business case has six parts:
1. The need: the problem or opportunity, with evidence.
2. Options: realistic responses, always including doing nothing.
3. Analysis: how each option performs on benefits, cost, risk and fit.
4. Recommendation: one option and why.
5. Costs and funding: the budget and the reserve.
6. Risks and assumptions that could change the answer.

Dr. Helen Marchetti (E-001), the executive sponsor, decides. Write for her: short, evidence first, plain words. A case that hides its weak points loses trust the first time someone finds them.

read.heading: The need, in Kestrel's numbers
read.body:
Each problem gets evidence from the baseline period (1 July to 30 September 2026).

| Problem | Evidence (data) |
|---|---|
| Patient flow | KGH median 80.5 minutes from arrival to physician initial assessment (PIA), against 45.5 at Prairie Gate. Left without being seen (LWBS) 5.7% across sites, 7.5% at KGH. Only 28.3% of assessed visits (126 of 445) seen within their Canadian Triage and Acuity Scale (CTAS) objective. |
| Trust in numbers | Emailed extracts disagree between sites and carry more patient detail than anyone needs. The emergency department (ED) extract alone has duplicates, impossible times and invalid dates. |
| Access | Only 27.3% of access requests resolved within 72 hours; median 4.26 days. Two missed leavers still enabled (E-014, E-027). Privileged accounts with multi-factor authentication (MFA): 66.7%. Q3 access reviews on time: 66.7%. |
| Resilience | Clinical Information System (CIS) restore tests failed at 9.0 and 13.5 hours against a 4-hour recovery time objective (RTO). Last test 2025-08-14, 413 days before 2026-10-01. Security awareness among agency and vendor workers: 48%. |

Evidence turns a complaint into a case. "Clinicians wait for access" invites debate; "27.3% of requests meet 72 hours" invites a decision.

read.heading: Options, including doing nothing
read.body:
Always compare at least three options. The do-nothing option is the baseline every other option must beat, and it is rarely free: its cost is the risk you keep.

| Criterion | A: Do nothing | B: Analytics only | C: Analytics and access | D: Full programme |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Trusted ED and bed figures | No | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Extracts limited to what is needed | No | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Access granted on day one, removed on the last day | No | No | Yes | Yes |
| Proven CIS recovery | No | No | No | Yes |
| Cost (CAD) | No project spend | 420,000 (Release 1) | 880,000 (Releases 1 and 2) | 1,200,000 plus 120,000 reserve |
| Delivery risk | Low | Medium | Medium | Higher, managed by one programme |

All four are costed from the same 15 work-package estimates, so the comparison is fair. Option B fixes the most visible problem but leaves the access and recovery risks the board asked about. Option C still leaves Kestrel unable to show it can recover the CIS. Option D costs more and asks more of the same people, but one charter, one schedule and one change-control board let Kestrel share staff and trade off across releases. The recommendation is D, with A kept honest as the comparison.

Two exam ideas live here. Sunk cost (money already spent) never justifies a choice. Opportunity cost is the value of the best option you did not choose.

read.heading: Benefits you can measure
read.body:
A benefit is an improvement someone values, measured against a baseline. Keep three words apart: an output is what the project produces (a dashboard); an outcome is the change it enables (leaders act on waits earlier); a benefit is the measurable gain (fewer patients leave unseen).

| Measure | Baseline (data) | Target (agreed) |
|---|---|---|
| Median minutes to PIA, KGH | 80.5 | 60 |
| LWBS rate, all sites | 5.7% | 4.5% |
| Access requests resolved within 72 hours | 27.3% | 80% |
| Median days to fulfil an access request | 4.26 | 1 |
| Missed leavers | 2 | 0 |
| Privileged accounts with MFA | 66.7% | 100% |
| Q3 access reviews on time | 66.7% | 100% |
| CIS restore within its 4-hour RTO | Failed | Pass |
| Security awareness, agency and vendor | 48% | 90% |

Each is measured three months after its release, because benefits arrive after delivery. Worked example (computed): Q3 had 474 valid visits. At 4.5% instead of 5.7%, LWBS would be about 474 x 0.045 = 21 visits instead of 27, so about six more patients a quarter would see a physician. Name a business owner for each benefit, such as Dr. Whitford for the ED measures, because the programme ends before most benefits are realized.

read.heading: Cost, reserve and financial tests
read.body:
The budget at completion (BAC) is CAD 1,200,000 across 15 work packages: Release 1 CAD 420,000, Release 2 CAD 460,000, Release 3 CAD 320,000. On top sits a management reserve of CAD 120,000 held by the sponsor, so total authorized funding is CAD 1,320,000.

Know the two kinds of reserve:
- Contingency reserve covers identified risks (known unknowns). It sits inside the cost baseline and the project manager uses it as planned responses are triggered.
- Management reserve covers unforeseen work (unknown unknowns). It sits outside the baseline, the sponsor controls it, and using it needs a change decision.

The exam also expects the classic financial tests. Net present value (NPV) discounts future cash flows to today; pick the higher NPV. Payback period is the time to recover the investment; shorter is better. A benefit-cost ratio above 1 means benefits exceed costs. Beacon's main benefits are patient flow, privacy compliance and safe recovery, which do not convert neatly to cash, so its case rests on measured outcomes and avoided risk rather than NPV.

read.heading: The risk and service case
read.body:
CISSP thinks about a business case as a risk decision. Management must show due care (doing what a reasonable organization would do) and due diligence (checking that it is done and works). Kestrel runs backups, which is care, but has not proven a restore in 413 days, so diligence is missing. A control is justified when the risk it reduces is worth more than it costs.

ITIL adds the service view. Value is co-created: Kestrel's analytics team, clinical leaders and the service desk produce it together, and consumers weigh the outcomes they gain against the costs and risks they take on. A dashboard nobody supports is a cost without a service, which is why Grace Liu (E-005) and the support model are in scope. The guiding principle Focus on value keeps every option tied to patients and clinicians.

The finished case lists all eight programme risks, R-01 to R-08, with owners. These five matter most to the choice of option:
- R-01 data quality undermines trust (Tomás Rivera, E-006).
- R-02 small counts at Prairie Gate could identify patients (Priya Raman, E-003).
- R-04 the CIS cannot be restored within 4 hours (Daniel Osei, E-004).
- R-05 Sentinel SOC Services processes security logs in the United States (Priya Raman).
- R-07 Lumen Analytics Partners' contract ends 2026-11-30 (Programme Manager).

keyTerms.definition: A document that justifies an investment by comparing options against a stated need, with benefits, costs, risks and a recommendation. It comes before the charter.
Says how, when and by whom each benefit is measured and realized, including after the programme closes.
The baseline option of continuing as today. Its cost is the risk and waste you keep, so every other option must beat it.
Funds for unforeseen work, outside the cost baseline and controlled by the sponsor. Beacon's is CAD 120,000; using it needs a change decision.
Funds inside the cost baseline for identified risks, used as planned responses are triggered.
Future cash flows discounted to today's value, minus the investment. When comparing projects on finance alone, choose the higher NPV.
Due care is acting as a reasonable organization would; due diligence is verifying that the controls exist and work, such as testing a restore.

steps: Open Project, Release 1, Business case. Read How to write it and See the finished example, and keep your programme brief open for the problem statements.

In the need section, build a table with the three problems and their evidence: 80.5 minutes median to PIA at KGH, 5.7% LWBS, 27.3% of access requests within 72 hours, two missed leavers, CIS restores of 9.0 and 13.5 hours against 4 hours.

In the options section, describe A do nothing, B analytics only (CAD 420,000), C analytics and access (CAD 880,000) and D the full programme (CAD 1,200,000 plus CAD 120,000 reserve), say what each leaves unsolved, and compare them in one table.
In the benefits section, list the nine measures with baseline labelled data, target labelled agreed, the three-month measurement point and a business owner for each.

In the cost section, show the release budgets (WP-101 to WP-115), the management reserve held by Dr. Marchetti and the total authorized CAD 1,320,000, and explain how reserve is released. On a refresh, add the earned value position: at 2026-10-01 the estimate at completion is CAD 1,342,500, CAD 22,500 above total authorized funding (R-08).

In the risks section, list R-01 to R-08 with their owners and the main risk of doing nothing. Then write the privacy, security and service value section: the Health Information Act duties (sections 57, 58 and 60), the privacy impact assessment submitted to the Commissioner before go-live (section 64), and why each release ends as a supported service.
Finish with a short recommendation asking the sponsor to approve option D with the charter, and record the decision as D-01 once it is made.
build.modelAnswer: A strong business case leads with a one-paragraph recommendation, then proves it. The need table uses only data figures. The options include doing nothing. Benefits separate outputs from outcomes and label each target as agreed. Release budgets add to CAD 1,200,000 and the reserve is shown separately. Each named risk has an owner.

examTips.tip: Process task 3 Help ensure value-based delivery and Business Environment task 1 Define and establish project governance: the business case and benefits plan come before the charter. If a question asks what justifies the project, the answer is the business case; what authorizes it is the charter.

Process task 6 Plan and manage finance: higher NPV wins, shorter payback wins, a benefit-cost ratio above 1 is favourable, and sunk costs are ignored. Management reserve is outside the cost baseline and needs sponsor approval to use.

Security and Risk Management, 1.9 risk management concepts and 1.7 Business Continuity requirements: management owns risk decisions. Your role is to advise with evidence, such as failed restore tests, so leaders can show due care and due diligence.

Focus on value and value co-creation: when an option delivers outputs but not the outcomes consumers want, or hides the costs and risks they must carry, it does not create value. Pick the answer that starts from the consumer's outcomes.

pitfalls: Leaving out the do-nothing option. Without it the sponsor cannot see what the investment buys compared with today.
Counting outputs as benefits. A dashboard is an output; fewer patients leaving unseen is the benefit, measured against the 5.7% baseline.
Mixing the reserve into the budget. BAC is CAD 1,200,000; the CAD 120,000 management reserve sits outside it and belongs to the sponsor.
Hiding risks to look stronger. Name the risks that could change the recommendation, each with an owner.

check.q: Why must the Beacon business case include a do-nothing option even though nobody wants it?
check.a: It is the baseline. It shows what Kestrel keeps if it does not invest: untrusted figures, over-detailed extracts, missed leavers and an unproven CIS restore. Every other option's benefits and costs are measured against it, so leaving it out hides the value of the investment.

check.q: What is the difference between Beacon's management reserve and a contingency reserve?
check.a: Contingency reserve sits inside the cost baseline for identified risks and the programme uses it as planned responses trigger. The CAD 120,000 management reserve sits outside the baseline for unforeseen work; Dr. Marchetti controls it and using it needs a change decision.

check.q: Which is the benefit: the ED dashboard, leaders acting on waits earlier, or LWBS falling from 5.7% to 4.5%?
check.a: LWBS falling from 5.7% to 4.5% is the benefit: a measurable gain against a data baseline. The dashboard is an output and leaders acting earlier is the outcome it enables. Benefits are measured three months after the release and owned by the business.

items.summary: You learn what a charter authorizes, how to write objectives and success criteria that can be tested, and how governance works in all four exams. You draft the Beacon programme charter that Dr. Helen Marchetti approved on 2026-09-01 as decision D-01.

read.heading: What a charter does
read.body:
The charter formally authorizes the programme. It names the Programme Manager, gives you authority to use Kestrel's people and money, and records what was agreed at the start. The sponsor issues it; you usually draft it. Without it, you are asking colleagues for favours.

The charter is short and high level. It links to the business case for justification and leaves detail to later plans: the scope statement, schedule and risk log you build next week. Once signed, it becomes a reference point. A change to its objectives, gates or budget goes through change control, never a quiet edit.

For Beacon, decision D-01 records that Dr. Helen Marchetti (E-001) approved the charter on 2026-09-01, the first day of the programme. That date is the first milestone in the schedule (task 2, Charter approved, zero duration). Every later decision traces back to it.

read.heading: What goes in the Beacon charter
read.body:
| Section | Beacon content |
|---|---|
| Purpose | The three problems in two or three sentences; link to the business case (BCN-R1-03), which recommends option D, the full programme |
| Objectives | One objective per release, then the nine success measures with baseline, agreed target, owner and measurement date (next section) |
| High-level scope | Release 1 analytics service, Release 2 identity and access, Release 3 cyber resilience; key exclusions |
| Milestones | Charter 2026-09-01; Release 1 go-live gate 2026-10-23; Release 2 acceptance 2026-11-26; programme acceptance 2026-12-17 |
| Budget | CAD 1,200,000 (420,000, 460,000, 320,000); management reserve CAD 120,000; total CAD 1,320,000 |
| Governance | Sponsor E-001; change-control board (CCB) chaired by Marcus Bell (E-002); privacy, Priya Raman (E-003); security, Daniel Osei (E-004) |
| Risks, assumptions, constraints | R-01 to R-08 at summary level |
| Success and exit criteria | How each release is accepted and when benefits are measured |
| Approval | Sponsor signature and D-01 |

Two tests for every line: could a new board member understand it, and could someone check later whether it happened? If not, rewrite it.

read.heading: Objectives and success criteria you can test
read.body:
Write objectives that are specific, measurable, achievable, relevant and time-bound (SMART). Compare:
- Weak: Improve ED flow at KGH.
- Strong: Reduce the median minutes from arrival to physician initial assessment at KGH from 80.5 (Q3 2026 baseline) to 60, measured three months after Release 1.

The charter carries the nine agreed targets from the business case, from left without being seen (LWBS) 5.7% to 4.5% through security awareness 48% to 90%. It also makes privacy and security part of success, not an afterthought:
- A privacy impact assessment is submitted to the Information and Privacy Commissioner for review and comment before Release 1 goes live. Under section 64 of the Health Information Act (HIA), a custodian must do this before implementing a practice or system involving individually identifying health information. The Commissioner comments; it does not approve.
- Dashboards use de-identified, aggregated data classified Confidential, and counts under 5 are suppressed outside the care team (Kestrel policy).
- Row-level security is proven by positive and negative tests for each site.
- Privileged accounts reach 100% multi-factor authentication (MFA) and the Clinical Information System (CIS) restore passes its 4-hour recovery time objective (RTO).

Each criterion names its evidence, so acceptance is a check, not an argument.

read.heading: Budget, reserve and your authority
read.body:
The charter sets the money and who may move it. The baseline is CAD 1,200,000 across 15 work packages. The sponsor holds the CAD 120,000 management reserve outside the baseline. Total authorized funding is CAD 1,320,000.

State your authority plainly. As Programme Manager you direct work, assign people within agreed work packages and report status. Beacon's charter sends three things to the change-control board, chaired by Marcus Bell: any change to scope, any change that moves a release gate, and any request to use management reserve, which also needs the sponsor. Clear limits protect you as much as Kestrel: nobody can later say you overstepped, and you know when to escalate.

Name the decision makers for the things that are not yours to decide. Priya Raman (E-003) approves the privacy impact assessment internally. Daniel Osei (E-004) advises on security risk; Dr. Marchetti, as sponsor, accepts residual risk on that advice. Dr. Whitford (E-007) and Janelle Cardinal (E-008) own the emergency and bed data and accept the dashboards built on it.

read.heading: Risks, assumptions and constraints
read.body:
The charter lists the high-level risks so the sponsor approves with eyes open. Details live in the RAID (risks, assumptions, issues, decisions) log you open next week.

| ID | Risk | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| R-01 | ED extract data quality undermines trust | Tomás Rivera (E-006) |
| R-02 | Small counts at PGH could identify patients | Priya Raman (E-003) |
| R-03 | MFA prompts slow clinicians at shared workstations | Janelle Cardinal (E-008) |
| R-04 | CIS cannot be restored within its 4-hour RTO | Daniel Osei (E-004) |
| R-05 | Sentinel SOC Services processes logs in the United States | Priya Raman (E-003) |
| R-06 | Key-person dependency on Tomás Rivera | Programme Manager |
| R-07 | Lumen Analytics Partners' contract ends 2026-11-30 | Programme Manager |
| R-08 | Cost performance could exhaust the reserve | Marcus Bell (E-002) |

A constraint is a limit you must work within: the gate dates, the budget, the HIA duties, Kestrel's small-count rule and Lumen's fixed-price contract. An assumption is something you treat as true without proof, such as the business owners being free for the six-day requirements task or Meridian Clinical Systems supporting the December restore test. Write assumptions down so you can test them, because a wrong assumption becomes a risk or an issue.

read.heading: Governance in all four exams
read.body:
Governance decides who directs and controls the work, and how decisions are made and recorded.

- PMP treats it as Business Environment task 1, Define and establish project governance: sponsor, board, decision rights, escalation paths and approval records.
- ITIL lists governance as one of the five components of the ITIL Value System, next to the guiding principles, value chain activities, management practices and continual improvement. Governance directs the organization; services are run within it.
- CISSP covers it in Security and Risk Management, 1.3 security governance principles: security serves the organization's goals, roles and responsibilities are defined, and senior management stays accountable for risk. The data owner decides classification and use; the custodian applies the controls.

In Beacon all three meet in one place: the charter approved as D-01, a change-control board with a named chair, and named owners for privacy, security and data. When an exam question asks who should decide, look for the role the governance gives that decision to.

keyTerms.definition: The document that formally authorizes the programme, names the Programme Manager and their authority, and records objectives, scope, milestones, budget, risks and approval.
An objective that is specific, measurable, achievable, relevant and time-bound, such as KGH median minutes to PIA from 80.5 to 60 three months after Release 1.
The group that decides changes to approved baselines. Beacon's is chaired by Marcus Bell (E-002).
A limit the programme must work within, such as the 2026-10-23 gate, the CAD 1,200,000 budget or a legal duty.
Something treated as true for planning without proof. It must be recorded and tested because a wrong assumption turns into a risk or issue.
A logged decision with ID, date, decision maker and rationale, such as D-01: charter approved by Dr. Helen Marchetti on 2026-09-01.

build.goal: Draft the Beacon programme charter: purpose, SMART objectives, high-level scope, milestones, budget and reserve, governance and authority, summary risks, assumptions and constraints, success criteria including privacy and security, and the D-01 approval.
steps: Open Project, Release 1, Programme charter. Read How to write it and See the finished example, with your business case beside it.

Write the purpose in two or three sentences that point to the business case and option D. Then write one objective per release in outcome language and the nine success measures with baseline (data), target (agreed), owner and measurement point.

Write high-level scope by release and an out-of-scope list (for example, replacing any clinical system, patient names on dashboards, real-time reporting), then a milestone table with the four dates from 2026-09-01 to 2026-12-17 and who decides each.
Add the budget table (Release 1 CAD 420,000, Release 2 CAD 460,000, Release 3 CAD 320,000), the CAD 120,000 management reserve held by the sponsor and the CAD 1,320,000 total.
